title: AGENT-COORDINATION
universal_lens: Agent coordination operates as a distributed state machine with asynchronous merge gates, where each agent's action space is defined by the global git HEAD and local PR queue, enabling parallelizable task execution without blocking on centralized merge authority.
gsi_mapping: GSI models agent progress through a conformal predictive state space, where each PR submission updates belief distributions over task completion times, using Bayesian priors derived from historical merge latency and code quality metrics.
gse_mapping: GSE encodes agent behavior as a Markov decision process over a shared repository state, where actions (push, PR, build) transition between observable states (unmerged, reviewed, merged) with stochastic rewards based on task throughput and concurrency efficiency.

primitives.name: Asynchronous Merge Gate
primitives.verbatim_quote: THE RULE THAT MATTERS MOST: never block on a merge You do **not** have merge authority and you do **not** need it.
primitives.assumptions: Merge authority is delegated to an autonomous agent (Claude session) operating on a fixed schedule.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When an agent waits for manual merge, it enters a stall state with zero progress.

layer2.mapping: The asynchronous merge gate mirrors a non-blocking semaphore in concurrent programming, where the agent's workflow continues independently of the merge event.
layer2.telemetry: PR creation time vs. merge time ratio, number of stalled runs per day.

primitives.name: Agent State Transition
primitives.verbatim_quote: **So: push a branch, open a PR, and immediately start the NEXT item.** Do not wait for the merge.
primitives.assumptions: Each agent maintains a local task queue and transitions between states via git operations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when an agent halts execution upon waiting for a merge confirmation.

layer2.mapping: Agent state transitions are modeled as a deterministic finite automaton with states {building, pushing, reviewing, merging} and actions {commit, push, open_pr, build_next}.
layer2.telemetry: Average time between push and next task initiation, percentage of runs without stalls.

primitives.name: Shared Git State
primitives.verbatim_quote: So always `git fetch origin main` and re-read this file at the start of a run — that is the only way you learn what changed.
primitives.assumptions: All agents synchronize their view of the repository through a single canonical reference point (main branch).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inconsistency arises when agents operate on stale branches without fetching latest changes.

layer2.mapping: The shared git state functions as a distributed consensus layer, where each agent's local workspace must align with the global commit history to prevent divergence.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of merge conflicts, number of outdated local branches.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that agent coordination is modeled as a decentralized workflow governed by asynchronous merge semantics. Each agent operates within a bounded task space defined by the repository's HEAD and their own PR queue. The system avoids deadlock by enforcing that no agent blocks on merge, instead transitioning directly to the next task. This creates a dualism between local execution and global synchronization, where the agent's internal state machine is decoupled from the merge gate. The failure mode emerges when agents attempt to synchronize on merge events, which introduces a temporal dependency that violates the asynchronous nature of the system. The shared git state ensures consistency across agents, but only if they actively fetch updates. Thus, the model becomes a hybrid of deterministic task scheduling and probabilistic merge timing, where the latter is abstracted into a stochastic process that does not impede forward progress.
